loop_control.rule: wrong rule: < vs <= and 0..n vs 0..n-1 are interchangeable. Right rule: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n.

paths.logic: i < n and i <= n mean the same, so the loop runs until i equals n and the last pass can use a[n].
paths.twin_logic: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n.

paths.label: correct
paths.logic: A loop prints the same thing on every pass; the changing loop variable does not affect what the body does.
paths.twin_logic: The body uses the current value of the loop variable, so its output can differ on each pass.
